rules.statement: In a test that checks the order of two text fragments in a generated file, assert the order (or adjacency with any whitespace allowed between them) rather than an exact character offset that depends on precise spacing.
rules.why: An exact offset such as `+ 1` makes a harmless reflow, line break or double space fail the suite with a misleading ordering message when the order is actually fine.
rules.check: Look for position checks in test code that compare an index to another index plus a text length plus a fixed constant; they should use `-lt`-style ordering comparisons or a regex allowing `\s+` between the fragments, and a comment should say whether adjacency is intended.

rules.statement: When a change rewords instruction or documentation text to fix a mismatch, add a test that requires the corrected wording so that the old wording can't come back unnoticed.
rules.why: Without an assertion on the rewritten sentence the suite stays green if the text reverts and the earlier mismatch returns.
rules.check: For diffs that change prose in generated instruction or template files to fix a reported mismatch, check that the template test suite asserts the key phrase of the new wording in that file.

rules.statement: Don't report a CHANGELOG section date only because it matches the date of the section below it or is a day off from today's UTC date.
rules.why: Sections are dated the day they were written in the author's local time zone, and several releases on the same day sharing a date is normal in the changelog.
rules.check: Before reporting, see whether other changelog sections already share dates and whether the gap from today is only a UTC versus local time-zone difference; report only a date that is clearly wrong.
